comments.author: @DexterGordon-dr8qd
comments.text: This AI rubbish just rehashes cliché's. It has very LITTLE to do with reality of living in the Netherlands. One example: Yes the Dutch have more bicycles than people, but the Netherlands is ALSO a very CAR-DENSE society. There is more than 1 car per household on average, and the large majority of the morning and afternoon commutes are done either by car (on a network of 2400 kilometers of modern multilane highways, in a country that only measures 120 by 200 miles...), or by a very well developed public transport network. And yes the Dutch DO USE their bikes (a lot) but that is for the shorter trips near home (to shop, school, etc.) Only people who are lucky enough to live with about 3 miles from work will also commute by bike.
